data.title: Conversation History
data.tagline: Conversation history is the earlier messages a product saves and can include again when they matter to a new request
data.learningOutcome: You can explain that continuous chat depends on the product bringing relevant earlier messages into the next request.
data.description: When you say “make the second one shorter,” the application retrieves the three earlier titles and includes the relevant material in this request. A complete transcript in the interface does not mean the model received every message this time.

learning.assumes: You have used a chat product that supports follow-up questions.
learning.outcome: You can explain that continuous chat depends on the product bringing relevant earlier messages into the next request.

explanation.title: The product saves old messages
explanation.text: The chat product can keep the three titles and later replies in its own records.

explanation.title: The application selects relevant parts
explanation.text: For this request, it retrieves the three titles and sends them with the new message.

explanation.title: The model sees only what was sent
explanation.text: If the request contains only “make the second one shorter,” visible UI history cannot resolve the reference.

data.boundary: Conversation history is what the product has saved. A stateless request still needs the relevant material supplied again. Saved does not mean sent.

lessonPractice.title: After a long chat, a user says Shorten the second one. All old messages are visible, but the model edits the wrong item. How should this improve?

options.label: Include the relevant list and reference in this request while limiting unrelated history
options.feedback: The model needs the referenced content to resolve second; visible history does not prove it was sent.

options.label: Always send the complete history without considering window, cost, or relevance
options.feedback: Full history continuously consumes space and cost and may let outdated goals interfere with the task.

options.label: Keep old messages visible in the UI and do not inspect whether the request includes them
options.feedback: Saving and displaying messages is separate from assembling model input, so one cannot replace the other.

data.agentPrompt: Before editing the second item, confirm the referenced list is in the current context and restate the target. Keep only relevant history and summarize older material; never assume visible UI messages were sent.
